newsitem.title: USA: February rains improve Oklahoma wheat condition.
newsitem.headline: February rains improve Oklahoma wheat condition.

text.p: Timely rains during February improved wheat conditions and replenished soil moisture, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its monthly winter crop report.
Oklahoma wheat condition was rated nine percent excellent, 74 good, 14 fair and three percent poor. That compared to last month's rating of five percent excellent, 69 good, 23 fair and three fair.
The report said southeastern areas of the state have received excessive amounts of rain over the last few weeks, causing flooding of some wheat.
The Panhandle district missed most of the rains and was in need of moisture for dryland wheat.
Insect pressure was reported to be light statewide.
Pasture conditions decreased slightly during the month but continued to be rated good to fair. Pasture conditions should improve as temperatures increase, the report said.
Cattle marketings are reported as above average, with many areas reporting heavy marketings as producers begin to pull cattle off wheat pasture. Hay supplies were adequate to short.
Soil moisture was rated adequate to surplus in most areas.
